mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of greater than 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand but a nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a mild equity pullback over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle consumer weakening with housing stabilization
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when the trigger is met in at least 5 out of the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer and corporate confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation risk, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate preemptive Fed hikes.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in triggered months over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to expected earnings downgrades.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.4% month-over-month, accompanied by a federal funds rate below 2%, signals inflationary pressure in a low-rate environment, which historically boosts S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate accommodative policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in triggered months over the last 15 years.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the trajectory of real GDP growth (GDPC1 quarter-over-quarter change) and S&P 500 20-day forward returns; higher GDP growth signals stronger corporate earnings momentum, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between GDPC1 qoq growth and S&P 500 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
